original_text: These parameters are chosen to reproduce the neutron pairing gap in neutron matter obtained in BCS calculations with a bare nuclear force in the ${}^1S_0$ channel.
injected_text: These parameters are chosen to reproduce the neutron pairing gap in neutron matter obtained in BCS calculations with a bare nuclear force.
rationale: The cited paper (Matsuo:2005vf) derives the pairing gap specifically in the ${}^1S_0$ partial-wave channel, an explicit scope qualifier; dropping '${}^1S_0$ channel' over-generalises the calibration claim to all partial-wave channels, which the cited paper does not support.
ground_truth_description: Removed the '${}^1S_0$ channel' qualifier from the sentence describing the pairing parameter calibration target, over-generalising a result that holds only for the singlet S-wave channel.

truth.claim_sentence_verbatim: These parameters are chosen to reproduce the neutron pairing gap in neutron matter obtained in BCS calculations with a bare nuclear force in the ${}^1S_0$ channel.

original_text: The resulting coupling strength is smaller than the estimate based on the hydrodynamical model of Ref.~\cite{Kobyakov:2013eta} by roughly a factor of five when the entrainment effect is neglected.
injected_text: The resulting coupling strength is smaller than the estimate based on the hydrodynamical model of Ref.~\cite{Kobyakov:2013eta} by roughly a factor of three when the entrainment effect is neglected.
rationale: Changing 'five' to 'three' in the Conclusion creates a percent_of inconsistency: the body (Discussion) reports the hydrodynamical value as 3.4×10⁴ MeV fm³ versus the microscopic result 7.1×10³ MeV fm³, a ratio of ~4.8 (factor of five), while the Conclusion now claims a factor of three (~33%), a relative discrepancy of >50% triggering a MAJOR upgrade.
ground_truth_description: The suppression factor in the Conclusion was changed from 'five' to 'three', inconsistent with the values 3.4×10⁴ and 7.1×10³ MeV fm³ reported in the Discussion (true ratio ≈ 4.8).
